provenance.what: A paid round of the acceptance test author's evaluation on the recorded web-calculator run (docs/features/protected-acceptance-tests/plan.md, Task 4).
provenance.consent: Operator, 2026-10-21: loop on paid rounds until the thresholds pass, up to $15 in total including Task 4's first $4.94.
provenance.control: bc57eb7482b4737fd1fe9e110e50652c630a0aa7's src/app.js with its Enter branch replaced: Enter always does equals, and on #theme-toggle the key's default is left to activate the control
provenance.dropped: Each dispatch's raw stream, tool log and prompt, and each suite run's full report log: kept only in the --out directory. Messages are cut to their first line.

thresholds:
Registered 2026-10-21, before any answer under the corrected control and lint was seen. A setting passes only if it meets all four:
1. Gate: at least 2 of 3 suites pass the validity gate.
2. Catches finding 9: in each gate-passing suite, at least one AC-018 test fails at b5d42890 and passes on the control.
3. Catches finding 10: in each gate-passing suite, at least one test under AC-013, AC-014, AC-015 or AC-024 fails at bc57eb74 and passes on the control.
4. Precision: no test fails on the control in a gate-passing suite. Each control failure is read by hand against the control's code; one that exposes a real control defect corrects the control and is re-scored, never discounted.

reply.summary:
Wrote three Playwright files under acceptance/web-calculator/: calculator.spec.mjs, keyboard.spec.mjs and theme-layout.spec.mjs. They are .mjs because the runner can't load top-level await from a .js file without a package.json. Together they cover every criterion except AC-010, which the specification doesn't define. I ran the three files with --repeat-each 2 against a throwaway reference page and all 218 tests passed. Against the blank index.html, the calculator file failed all 22 tests on locator waits or assertions, never on navigation. I ran the keyboard and theme-layout files only against the reference page, not the blank page, because the failing tests are slow and the first blank-page run hit the time ceiling. I deleted the reference page afterwards, so no index.html is left.

- **Calculator and AC-023:** Tests for AC-001 to AC-012 and AC-023 click through the sequences, with AC-002 run once per digit 0 to 9. The display check follows the specification's definition of "shows the value", rejecting a match next to a digit, decimal point or minus sign.
- **Keyboard:** AC-013 to AC-017 and AC-024 each run with focus on the document body and on each kind of focusable element: a digit button, an operator, equals, clear, backspace and the theme control. A button that also reacted to Enter or Backspace would double-act and fail. One extra test checks that Enter with focus on the theme control both does equals and toggles the theme.
- **Theme (AC-018 to AC-020):** AC-018 runs by click, by Enter and by Space on the focused control. AC-019 and AC-020 close the page and reopen a new one in the same context.
- **Layout (AC-021):** Runs at 320×568. It checks that scrollWidth equals clientWidth, which is slightly stricter than "at most 320". It also checks that every button, the display and the theme control sit within 0 to 320.
- **Hover and focus (AC-022):** Runs once per control, 18 calculator buttons plus the theme control, in the light and dark themes. Each run compares a hover state and a Tab-focused state with the default state across the six listed style properties.

The tests assume the plan's element names: `#theme-toggle` for the theme control and role `status` for the display.

reply.summary:
I wrote three Playwright files under acceptance/web-calculator/: arithmetic.spec.mjs, keyboard.spec.mjs and theme-layout.spec.mjs. They are .mjs, not .js, because the runner failed to load .js files that start with a top-level await. Every criterion AC-001 to AC-024 (there is no AC-010) has at least one test titled with its ID.

- **arithmetic.spec.mjs:** AC-001 to AC-009, AC-011, AC-012 and AC-023. AC-002 has one test per digit 0 to 9.
- **keyboard.spec.mjs:** AC-013 to AC-017 and AC-024. Each is run with focus on the document body, then on a digit, decimal, operator, equals, clear, backspace and theme-control button. That checks the page-wide keys hold together with a focused button's own Enter behaviour.
- **theme-layout.spec.mjs:**
  - AC-018 is activated by click, Enter and Space, with body background-color compared between themes.
  - AC-019 and AC-020 close the page and open a new one in the same context.
  - AC-021 runs at 320×568.
  - AC-022 covers hover and Tab focus for all 19 buttons in the light and dark themes.

Against the blank index.html, all 77 tests fail on a locator action or an assertion, none on navigation. I then ran them against a throwaway implementation I wrote for the check. 76 passed and one failed: AC-018 activated by Enter on the theme control. It fails because that implementation cancels the Enter keydown for equals, which stops the focused button from activating. Enter must still toggle the theme while focus is on the theme control, so the implementer will need to handle that. The criterion allows any way of activating the control, so I kept the test. I deleted the throwaway index.html and left only the three test files.

Two choices you may want to know about:
- **Name matching:** the theme control is found by the name pattern /theme|dark|light/i, and the backspace button by /backspace|delete|⌫/i.
- **AC-022 properties:** the test picks whichever of the six listed style properties actually differs in the hovered or focused state. It then asserts that property with `not.toHaveCSS`.

reply.summary:
I wrote three Playwright files under acceptance/web-calculator/: calculator.spec.mjs (AC-001 to AC-009, AC-011 to AC-017, AC-023, AC-024), theme.spec.mjs (AC-018 to AC-020) and layout.spec.mjs (AC-021, AC-022). AC-010 does not appear in the specification, so it has no test. I used the .spec.mjs extension so the required top-level await works.

I ran the tests against a throwaway mock calculator at index.html, with --repeat-each 2. Everything in calculator.spec.mjs and layout.spec.mjs passed. In theme.spec.mjs only the Enter-key variants of AC-018, AC-019 and AC-020 failed. The mock's page-wide Enter handler calls preventDefault, so Enter does not activate a focused theme control. That is the conflict the tests are meant to catch.

I also ran every file once, without --repeat-each, against the blank index.html. Every test failed on an assertion or on a locator action that found no element, none on navigation. I deleted index.html afterwards.

- **Keyboard criteria (AC-013 to AC-017, AC-024):** each is checked with focus on the document body, on the theme control and on each of the 18 calculator buttons, with a fresh page load per target.
- **Theme control (AC-018 to AC-020):** each is activated by click, by Enter and by Space while it has keyboard focus. The persistence tests close the page and open a new page in the same browser context.
- **Layout (AC-021):** I set a 320×568 viewport and check that `scrollWidth` equals 320. That equals "at most 320" because the viewport is 320 wide. Every button, the display and the theme control must lie fully in the viewport.
- **Hover and focus states (AC-022):** separate hover and Tab-focus tests, each run in the light and dark themes, over all 19 controls.
- **Locators:** the display is found as role `status` and the backspace button by a name matching backspace, delete or ⌫, both taken from the plan. The theme control is found as a button whose name matches theme, dark or light. That name is my guess, because the plan gives only its id and says it has an aria-label.

tests.title: AC-001 Opening index.html from the local filesystem as a file:// URL in a current Chromium-based or Firefox browser, with no server process running, displays the calculator, and clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 15

AC-002 For each digit d from 0 through 9, after a fresh page load, clicking the button labelled 1 and then the button labelled d results in the display area showing the value formed by the digit 1 followed by d
AC-003 The page shows operator buttons labelled +, -, × and ÷, a decimal point button labelled ., an equals button labelled =, a clear button labelled C, and a backspace/delete button
AC-004 After a fresh page load, clicking the buttons 1, 2 in sequence results in the display area showing the value 12
AC-005 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 15
AC-006 After a fresh page load, clicking 7, -, 1, 0, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value -3
AC-007 After a fresh page load, clicking 6, ×, 7, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 42
AC-008 After a fresh page load, clicking 8, ÷, 2, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 4
AC-009 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, ., 5, +, 2, ., 2, 5, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 3.75

AC-011 After a fresh page load, clicking 5, +, 3 and then C results in the display area showing exactly the same text it showed on the fresh page load, and then clicking 2, +, 2, = results in the display area showing the value 4
AC-012 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, 2, 3 and then the backspace/delete button results in the display area showing the value 12 and its text not containing 123
AC-013 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 9, *, 3, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 27
